definitions.explanation: A supernatural being that has transformed or shapeshifted — ghosts, spirits, and creatures from Japanese folklore that take on different forms. Derived from {化|ば}ける (to transform).
Used figuratively for a person with extraordinary, almost inhuman abilities or characteristics — often in admiration of exceptional talent or physical capability.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{屋敷|やしき}に{化|ば}け{物|もの}が{出|で}る。
examples.english: Monsters appear in the old mansion.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}、{化|ば}け{物|もの}の{話|はなし}が{怖|こわ}かった。
examples.english: When I was a child, I was scared of monster stories.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{昔話|むかしばなし}には{様々|さまざま}な{化|ば}け{物|もの}が{登場|とうじょう}する。
examples.english: Various monsters appear in Japanese folktales.

examples.japanese: あの{選手|せんしゅ}は{化|ば}け{物|もの}だ。
{化|ば}け{物|もの}みたいな{体力|たいりょく}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}だ。
{彼女|かのじょ}の{記憶力|きおくりょく}は{化|ば}け{物|もの}じみている。

notes:
From {化|ば}ける (to transform) + {物|もの} (thing). In Japanese folklore, {化|ば}け{物|もの} specifically refers to creatures that shapeshift or transform, such as fox and tanuki spirits. Broader than {幽霊|ゆうれい} (ghost of a dead person).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{化|ば}け{物|もの}が{出|で}る (a monster appears)
・{化|ば}け{物|もの}みたいな (monster-like, freakish)
・{化|ば}け{物|もの}じみている (freakish, monstrous)
・{化|ば}け{物|もの}{屋敷|やしき} (haunted house)
